title: Unregistered sale agreements - the enforceability questions
p1: A signed property sale agreement feels like a guarantee. But what happens when that agreement was never registered? Many buyers discover this question only when a dispute appears.
p2: A common misconception is that an unregistered sale agreement is automatically worthless. The reality can be more complex. In many situations, such an agreement may still show that both parties had a deal, but it may not provide the same legal strength or benefits as a properly registered document.
p3: The key point is that signing a paper and having a legally protected transaction are not always the same thing. Registration rules, the type of property, and the purpose for which the document is being used can change the outcome. A small step like checking registration requirements before signing can prevent major problems later.
conclusion: Have you ever come across an unregistered sale agreement? Do you think a signed document should always be enough to protect the buyer?
